subject: Scratchplane quotas, I/O throttling, and blockstore binding for NorthShore private cluster
messages:
From: Tom Riley <triley@northshorehealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: ops@northshorehealth.com
Date: 2029-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: on-prem plan question - scratch storage quotas and eviction

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our infra team about how we should carve tenant scratch for ML preprocessing jobs:

- We expect a mix of short-lived bursty jobs and long-lived batch ETL; want to enforce a per-tenant scratch quota while still allowing short bursts.
- Concern about pods being evicted mid-run; need guidance on eviction thresholds and whether Guaranteed QoS is required for certain workloads.
- Curious about PV binding modes (Immediate vs WaitForFirstConsumer) because our racks have asymmetric NVMe capacity.

Can Redwood help with recommended node class layout (scratch-only nodes vs mixed), kubelet eviction settings, and any CSI/blockstore setup you recommend?

Also attaching our capacity spreadsheet for a rough sense of disk distribution.

Appreciate it —
Tom Riley
VP, Platform Operations
NorthShore Health

Attachment: nshore-capacity-2029Q2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Tom Riley <triley@northshorehealth.com>, ops@northshorehealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2029-04-03T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: on-prem plan question - scratch storage quotas and eviction

Hi Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. I sketched a practical pattern below that balances isolation, cost, and eviction risk. High level: provide a distinct "scratchplane" node class for tenant ephemeral workloads, use CSI with topology-aware PVs and WaitForFirstConsumer for NVMe affinity, and enforce tenant quotas via a combination of ResourceQuota for PersistentVolumeClaims + a lightweight admission webhook to cap aggregate ephemeral usage. Details: 

1) Node classes and taints
- scratchplane-nvme (taint: scratch-only=true:NoSchedule) — fast NVMe, preemptible/ephemeral nodes for bursty jobs.
- compute-standard (general purpose) — long-lived services, small ephemeral volumes.
- guarantee-nodes (Guaranteed QoS) — for jobs you promise not to evict (e.g., nightly training checkpointing)

2) PV binding and topology
- Use CSI driver with TopologyAware provisioning; set StorageClass with volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer to ensure PVC lands in the rack with NVMe.
- Create StorageClasses: scratch-fast (local-NVMe), scratch-fallback (remote-blockstore with lower IOPS).

3) Quota & admission controls
- ResourceQuota per namespace for number of PVCs and total requested storage. This prevents runaway claims.
- Admission webhook that implements a per-tenant live-usage cap (counts ephemeral directory usage or ephemeral PVCs) to allow burst above quota for short windows (e.g., 10 minutes) but reject sustained exceed.

4) Eviction and kubelet tuning
- For scratchplane nodes: raise eviction thresholds for ephemeral-storage to avoid aggressive OOM-style evictions; prefer soft eviction with grace period for short bursts.
- For critical long jobs, schedule onto guarantee-nodes with Guaranteed QoS class (requests==limits).

5) I/O throttling and cgroup controls
- Use cgroup v2 io controller on nodes to set per-cgroup throttles for tenant pods; combine with node-level eBPF observability to detect noisy neighbors.

6) Blockstore binding & fallback strategy
- PVCs default to scratch-fast; if capacity exhausted, PVCs can be provisioned into scratch-fallback automatically via a StorageClass fallback controller we recommend including.

I've attached a short proposal and a PV binding matrix (requested). If you want, we can run a short PoC that simulates burst patterns and observe eviction rates with two configuration variants.

Proposed next step: quick 30-min ops workshop with your infra leads + our delivery engineer (Laura) to finalize node counts and eviction guardrails. Are you available next Tue or Wed?

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: nshore-scratchplane-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF stub)

Subject: Re: Initial: on-prem plan question - scratch storage quotas and eviction

Tom —

Short answers to your clarifications and a few operational notes for the workshop: 

1) Admission webhook behavior
- Yes, implement graded responses: if within PVC quota but IO over a short window, webhook returns a "soft-approve" that marks the pod with a label (redwood.io/burst=true) and an attached runtime policy that triggers cgroup io limits. If burst persists beyond the grace window, webhook will start rejecting new pod creations for that tenant until usage drops.

2) WaitForFirstConsumer & pre-created PVCs
- Pattern: let pre-created PVCs use a lightweight placeholder StorageClass (fast-reserve) that claims minimal metadata but is backed by a lazily-provisioned volume. At scheduling time, controller promotes the placeholder to a real volume and binds to the appropriate topology. This avoids long queueing delays while keeping topology correctness.

3) Metrics & SLOs to monitor in PoC
- per-tenant iops, throughput, percentiles for pod startup time (to catch provisioning delays), eviction_count, and reclaim latency for placeholder promotion.

4) DevOps checklist for workshop
- Share node inventory and rack-topology (we already asked for the spreadsheet).
- Decide preemption policy for scratchplane nodes (preemptible with 5-minute drain) and max burst window.

If workshop confirms these, we'll produce an ops runbook for tenant lifecycle (provision -> burst -> fallback -> reclaim). I'll prepare the draft runbook and the PV binding matrix for the meeting.

Happy to join Wed 2029-04-10 14:00 ET; send calendar invite.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Principal Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
